title: Sprite sheet freelancer experts needed
author: AnxiousInterest4219
selftext:
Hi All,

I want to generate a high quality sprite sheet for a human boy character for my preschool app.

And that character will have 15 emotions or animations. Those should be high quality ones

My road map is to have 10 such characters and if someone willing to work with me pls DM me.

Happy to discuss on the budget

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
Using a normal AI model like Nano Banana wont work for assets such as spritesheets and pixel art, because AI models cant output transparency, and image models alone have no understanding of animation.

That gap is actually why I built GameLab Studio ([https://gamelabstudio.co](https://gamelabstudio.co/?ref=reddit.com)). It’s designed for game assets, and it’ll generate consistent pixel-art sprites, animations and full transparent bg spritesheets for anything. Animations aren’t locked to walk/idle either; you can generate attack, fire, spin, explode, transform, whatever the gameplay needs.

https://preview.redd.it/dm0zitfdx9sg1.png?width=992&format=png&auto=webp&s=aed663a60fb6265648a49fe72ca495906556083f

It also enforces consistency across scale, palette, and angles, by using already generated angles of the same asset for reference, so you don’t end up with “AI asset soup” during prototyping.

We also have a seamless tileable edge-aware texture generation model

comments.author: AnxiousInterest4219
comments.body: Thanks for the info but I am looking for some jig resolution sprite sheet. Will this app help me ? Or restricted only to pixel art

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body: Yes, the app is not limited to pixel art. Any style of art can be generated. Additionally, we support resolutions up to 1024x1024 and 1920x1080

replies.author: AnxiousInterest4219
replies.body: Cool I will check this. And I need to add emotions like eating, sleeping and all human emotion. Will I be able to do or only limited to combat?

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
Awesome! Let me know if you have any questions or feature suggestions.

Yes, the workflow works like this: 
1. create base image for a given view angle (front) 
2. Create multiple animations for that angle
3. Export those animations to spritesheet


Optional:

4. Create other base image angles using the first one as reference to maintain coherence
5. Create animations for other angles
6. Export those to spritesheet

replies.author: AnxiousInterest4219
replies.body: Cool I will check this out and provide my feedback.

replies.author: AnxiousInterest4219
replies.body: May I know the pricing? Can we get free credit to try

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body: Yes, you start with 20 free credits which can make 20 images for instance

replies.author: AnxiousInterest4219
replies.body:
I tried and the tool is great for me to start.
If I create say 15 animation for a single character can I create one master sprite sheet?

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body: Awesome! Glad to hear you found it helpful. That’s a good question actually. Currently you would have to just combine them manually with copy paste into an image editor, but that’s actually a great idea for a feature to add. Thank you
